name: Booker T. & the M.G.'s
hook: The Stax house band: two Black and two white musicians in segregated Memphis, who had a hit by jamming while waiting for a singer and then played on hundreds of soul records.
blurb: Booker T. & the M.G.'s were the house band at Stax Records in Memphis: Booker T. Jones on organ, Steve Cropper on guitar, Lewie Steinberg on bass (replaced by Donald 'Duck' Dunn in 1965) and Al Jackson Jr. on drums. On a Sunday in June 1962, 17-year-old Jones and the others were waiting in the studio for a session with Billy Lee Riley that did not happen, and started jamming on an organ riff. That jam became 'Green Onions'. Jim Stewart wanted another song, 'Behave Yourself', as the A-side, but Cropper and Memphis DJs pushed 'Green Onions', and it went to number one R&B and number three pop. With two Black members and two white members at a time when Memphis was segregated, and in a genre then seen as Black, they were one of the first racially integrated groups in American pop. They played on hundreds of records by Otis Redding, Wilson Pickett, Sam & Dave and others, including 'I've Been Loving You Too Long', 'Try a Little Tenderness', 'Hold On, I'm Comin'' and 'Soul Man', and with Motown's Funk Brothers are credited with creating much of the sound of soul. Al Jackson Jr. was murdered in 1975. Dunn died in 2012 and Cropper in December 2025. Booker T. Jones later produced Willie Nelson's album 'Stardust' (1978).
